checks.primaryClaim: 30 days in total for a fresh licence, built up as 20 days for the Inspector's physical inspection + 5 days JCF review + 5 days CAF final approval, per the ED record (minDays 30, maxDays 30).
checks.sourceSays: The Labour Department's own Business Reforms Action Plan supporting document BRAP-130 ('Registration and Grant/Renewal of License for Factories') sets out, at row 7 'Procedure for getting Approval / NOC/ Licence/ Registration': "Inspector of Factories inspects the factory for verification. If found as per the plans approved by CIF, forwards the application to Chief Inspector of Factories through Joint Chief Inspector of Factories for approval. Inspection - 20 days  Forwarding - 5 days  Approval - 5 days", and at row 8 'Time Limit (Number of days)': "30 days". This is a stage-by-stage match to the ED's 20+5+5 breakdown and to its 30-day total. Independently corroborated by two further official documents fetched this session: (a) the Chief Inspectorate's own process-flow sheet, which ends with "Timeline :- Maximum Number of Days to complete application :- 30 days" (https://labour.py.gov.in/sites/default/files/lrdcifbprocessflowdiagramgrantrenewalamendmenttransferoflicence.pdf), and (b) Order No. 1234/CIF &B/83/2019 of the Office of the Chief Inspector of Factories & Boilers, 'Fixation of Timeline for processing of Application', which at Sl. No. 2 prescribes for "Registration and grant of licence for the new factories" (Form 2, Chief Inspector of Factories) a time limit of "Within one month from the date of receipt of application complete in all respects" (https://labour.py.gov.in/sites/default/files/fixation-timeline-processing-application-under-factories-act-1948-and-indian-boilers-act-1923..pdf); the same table is reproduced on the department's 'Time Bound Clearances' web page.

checks.primaryClaim: ED record: 'No flat fee; slab-based, auto-calculated by machinery HP rating and workforce size, levied annually with multi-year payment allowed, paid via the online GRAS (Government Receipt Accounting System); no separate fee for site inspection.' The ED explicitly flagged as MISSING: 'Exact fee slab table (by HP rating/workforce band) not given beyond example figures (Rs. 7,200/year, Rs. 14,400/2 years).'
checks.sourceSays: BRAP-130 Annexure II reproduces the full statutory schedule the ED could not supply: "Rule 4/ Rule 6 - GRANT/RENEWAL OF LICENCE FOR A FACTORY - SCHEDULE", a 12-row x 11-column matrix of "Total Horse Power Installed inclusive of Mobile equipments" (rows: Nil HP; Upto 10 HP; Above 10 HP upto 50 HP; Above 50 HP upto 129 H.P; Above 129 HP upto 250 HP; Above 250 HP upto 500 HP; Above 500 HP upto 1000 HP; Above 1000 HP upto 2000 HP; Above 2000 HP upto 5000 HP; Above 5000 HP upto 7500 HP; Above 7500 HP upto 10000 HP; Above 10000 HP) against "Maximum number of persons to be employed on any day during the year" (columns: 9, 20, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, Above 10000), "Fees payable in Rupees" - running from Rs. 800 (Nil HP, up to 9 persons) to Rs. 4,32,000 (Above 10000 HP, above 10000 persons); e.g. 'Above 10 HP upto 50 HP' x 500 persons = Rs. 28,800. The same document states at row 6 'Fee & Mode of Payment': "As per rule 4 ( Table under Annexure II) through online portal https://gras.py.gov.in", confirming the ED's GRAS claim, and the schedule's two axes (installed horse power and maximum persons employed) confirm the ED's 'slab-based by HP rating and workforce size' description. The multi-year option the ED describes is grounded in rule 6(3-A) as substituted by the Puducherry Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2020: "the fee payable for grant of or renewal of licence of a factory shall be proportionate to the annual fee as multiplied by number of years for which licence is sought for." No separate inspection fee appears anywhere in the schedule, consistent with the ED. CAVEAT: the department publishes three mutually inconsistent versions of this same licence-fee schedule (see remarks).

checks.primaryClaim: ED record: deemedApproval.status = 'no', days = null - 'No deemed approval provision exists for fresh licenses, mainly because the fee-payment (GRAS) portal and the licensing portal are not integrated, and because physical verification of machinery/layout/safety cannot be auto-cleared.'
checks.sourceSays: Rule 4(1) of the Puducherry Factories Rules, 1964, as published by the Labour Department itself (scanned rule text at page 14, with the proviso highlighted by the department), provides a deemed licence for a FRESH grant: "No premises shall be used as a factory nor any manufacturing process carried on in any factory except under and in accordance with the registration and licence granted under these rules; and Provided that if a valid application for grant of licence has been submitted and the required fees has been paid the premises shall be deemed to be fully licenced until such dates as the Chief Inspector grants the licence or refuses in writing to grant licence." The Labour Department's B-Easy (Ease of Doing Business) page links to this very document under its own descriptive title, citing it as the state's deemed-approval compliance: "Puducherry Factory Rules,1964 where rule 4(1) states that licence is deemed to be granted until returned by CIF. In Case of renewal under Rule 6(4) - page 18 states that lilcence is deemed to renewed until returned." So an official source states that a deemed-licence provision DOES exist for fresh grant, directly against the ED's 'no'. It is open-ended rather than day-bounded (it runs until the Chief Inspector grants or refuses in writing), so the ED's 'days: null' remains correct for fresh grant. For RENEWAL there is now an express 30-day deemed approval: rule 6(4), as substituted by the Puducherry Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2020 - final notification, G.O. Ms. No. 03/2020/Lab. dated 26th February 2021 - reads "If, the application has been made in accordance with this rule, the licence for the premises shall be deemed to have been automatically renewed for the applied period and an electronic certificate of registration/renewal shall be auto generated and issued after a period of 30 days from the date of submission of the application or until such date as the Chief Inspector may pass orders seeking clarifications on the application for the renewal."

checks.primaryClaim: ED record lists five items: duly filled application submitted online; statutory fee auto-calculated and paid online; list of proposed workers; land ownership proof or valid lease deed if leased; Pollution Control clearance for hazardous processes (obtained separately). ED separately flags that 'the documentation currently required is viewed as more extensive than necessary'.
checks.sourceSays: The Chief Inspectorate's official 'Checklist for Grant / Renewal / Amendment / Transfer of Licence' (page 2 of the process-flow document) lists: "1. Form 2, duly filled and signed the Occupier and Manager  2. Checklist  3. SBI paid Challan receipt for proof of Licence Fees  4. Original Stability certificate ( in case of Fresh and Amendment in HP / revision made in the plans)  5. Details of List of workers, indicating their address, age and nature of work ( in the case of Fresh application )  6. Details of Occupier [(a) Partnership and NOC from other partners nominating Occupier (b) Memorandum of Articles in case of Limited Companies supplemented by, Copy of Form 32 submitted to Registrar of Companies (proof of Director) & Board resolution nominating any one of Directors as Occupier (c) Appointment Letter of concerned administrative department - for Occupier of Government owned factories]  7. Valid Lease deed for the premises  8. Valid NOC / Consent issued by PPCC  9. Test Certificate obtained from competent persons in compliance to Rule 58, 59 & 60  10. Form 16A - Record of pre medical and periodical medical examination, in the case of hazardous process / Dangerous operation." Every ED-listed item maps onto this list (application = item 1; fee = item 3; list of proposed workers = item 5; lease deed = item 7; pollution-control clearance = item 8), so the ED list is confirmed but is a subset: the official checklist adds the stability certificate, occupier/constitution documents, rule 58-60 test certificates and Form 16A medical records. BRAP-130 Annexure III gives a shorter official list for the same service: "1. Form 2 duly filled in and signed by the occupier and manager  2. Remittance of license fee in commensurate with number of workers and motive power (as per annexure II)  3. Stability Certificate obtained from competent person / institution, recognized by the Chief Inspector of Factories, Puducherry.  4. Compliance to other conditions of the plan approval, which includes submission of Test Certificate in case of special machines.  5. List of workers proposed to be engaged.  6. Declaration of the occupier in the case of organizations other than proprietary concern." No official source found addresses the FGD claim that applicants must prepare seven sets/copies of documents.

checks.primaryClaim: ED record: eight steps - online filing via 'Government of India e-Factory licensing portal, customised for Puducherry' (portal URL null in the record); scrutiny by the Inspector; fee auto-calculated and paid online; physical inspection by the Inspector within 20 days for fresh licences only; offline inspection report; forwarding to the Joint Chief Inspector of Factories; JCF to Chief Inspector of Factories; CAF grants final approval. automationLevel 'partial'; applicantOfficeVisit 'no'.
checks.sourceSays: Online, no office visit: Order No. 4654/CIF &B/B5/2022 of the Office of the Chief Inspector of Factories & Boilers, dated 2 June 2022, states "As required under BRAP, 2021 the following services of Registration and Renewal of Licence for Factories under the Factories Act, 1948 are to be provided through online mode only" and "The services shall be availed through online mode only to eliminate the need to submit the applications physically, payment of fees for the services and track their status in each stage. On approval, the final certificate can be downloaded from the online portal anytime." (It adds that "Further Amendments to license will continue to be issued in Physical mode until the Online Application for Amendment to Factory License is launched.") Inspection and the approval chain: BRAP-130 states "Inspector of Factories inspects the factory for verification. If found as per the plans approved by CIF, forwards the application to Chief Inspector of Factories through Joint Chief Inspector of Factories for approval" - matching the ED's inspect -> IF -> JCF -> CIF sequence; the Chief Inspectorate's process-flow diagram shows the same chain with a split by size ("Upto 20 workers :- Assistant Inspector of Factories" / "More than 20 workers :- Inspector of Factories"), then "Inspection of the factory", "Licence application sent to Joint Chief Inspector of Factories", "Licence application forwarded to Chief Inspector of Factories", "Licence issued and sent to the Occupier of the Factory", with query loops at each stage. Portal identity (ED record had url: null): BRAP-130 row 9 'Form Submission' gives "Portal(https://serviceonline.gov.in/) to be accessed through the website of Labour Department, Puducherry (https://labour.py.gov.in)" - serviceonline.gov.in is the central ServicePlus platform, which substantiates the ED's description of a Government of India platform customised for Puducherry; the department publishes a matching 'Serviceplus - Registration/Renewal of Licence under Factories Act,1948 - Step by Step Guidelines' under BRAP #112 citing the same URL. Fee payment is on a separate portal ("through online portal https://gras.py.gov.in"), consistent with the ED's finding that GRAS and the licensing portal are not integrated. One nuance against the ED's fully-online framing: the statutory rule itself, as finally notified by the Puducherry Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2018 (G.O. Ms. No. 07/2019/Lab. dated 8 August 2019), still permits paper filing - "The application in Form No. 2 shall be made through the on-line portal of the Chief Inspectorate of Factories and Boilers, Puducherry, or personally delivered to the Office of the Chief Inspectorate of Factories and Boilers or sent by registered post" - so online-only rests on the 2022 administrative order rather than on the rules.

remarks: HIGHEST-VALUE FINDING (deemedApproval, contradicted): the ED record states flatly that no deemed approval exists for fresh factory licences in Puducherry, but the Labour Department's own B-Easy / Ease-of-Doing-Business page cites rule 4(1) of the Puducherry Factories Rules, 1964 as exactly that provision, and the rule text the department hosts carries the proviso highlighted: a valid application plus paid fees means 'the premises shall be deemed to be fully licenced until such dates as the Chief Inspector grants the licence or refuses in writing'. The deeming is open-ended (no day count), so it does not create a fixed-day clock the way an EoDB deemed-approval metric normally implies, and it operates as a right-to-operate-while-pending rather than as auto-issue of a licence; that may be why the issuing official described it as 'no'. For renewals the position is unambiguous and day-bounded: rule 6(4), as substituted by the Puducherry Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2020 (final notification G.O. Ms. No. 03/2020/Lab., dated 26 February 2021, gazetted 2 March 2021), gives automatic renewal with an auto-generated electronic certificate after 30 days.

FEE SCHEDULE CONFLICT - reviewers should not quote a Puducherry factory licence fee without saying which document it comes from. The Labour Department publishes three mutually inconsistent versions of the same Rule 4/6 licence-fee schedule on its own website, each roughly double the previous one: (a) the HTML page 'Approval, Licensing and Registration of a Factory' still prints the schedule 'with effect from 18th October, 2002 (G.O.Ms.No.33/2002/AIL/Lab./G)', running Rs. 200 to Rs. 1,08,000 (page last updated 28-01-2020); (b) the downloadable 'Fees Payable under Factories Act, 1948' PDF linked from the 'Fees Under Factories Act, 1948' page runs Rs. 400 to Rs. 2,16,000 - exactly double (a), and carries no notification reference or date in its text (PDF created Nov 2018, modified Jan 2020); (c) BRAP-130 Annexure II runs Rs. 800 to Rs. 4,32,000 - double (b) and quadruple (a). BRAP-130 is the most recent and is the document the department filed as its Business Reforms Action Plan evidence, so it is cited above as current, but no gazette notification establishing schedule (c) was located this session. The same three-way problem affects the plan-approval scrutiny fee: the HTML page says Small Scale Rs. 100 / Medium Rs. 500 / Large Rs. 1000, while BRAP-130 Annexure II says Rs. 250 / Rs. 2000 / Rs. 5000.

The ED's illustrative fee of Rs. 7,200 per year is a genuine cell in the schedule under both reading (a) and reading (c) - under (c) it is, for example, the fee for a Nil-HP factory employing up to 250 persons, or for an 'Above 250 HP upto 500 HP' factory employing up to 9 persons - so the ED's example is internally plausible and was not treated as contradicted.

VALIDITY (not one of the five checked keys, but a clear divergence worth flagging). The ED record says the licence is 'granted for a period chosen by the applicant, up to 10 years', and the FGD record shows business participants asking for validity to be 'increased to 5 years'. The binding rule says the opposite of a 10-year ceiling: rule 6(3-A) as substituted by the final Puducherry Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2020 reads 'Every Licence granted or renewed under this rule shall remain valid or be in force for a minimum period of ten years or more as applicable' - ten years is the statutory MINIMUM, with a proviso allowing the Chief Inspector to issue a shorter licence only for temporary factories or where the nature of activity demands it. (The earlier 2018 amendment, finally notified in August 2019, had permitted an optional multi-year payment 'for a period up to fifteen consecutive calendar years'; the unamended 1964 rule allowed up to three years.) This makes the FGD's request for 5-year validity a direct indicator that the 2021 ten-year-minimum rule is not reaching applicants in practice - the FGD gap flagged 'INCONSISTENT' on exactly this point is resolved in favour of the rule, not the participants' understanding.

TIMELINE is unusually well corroborated for this state: three separate official documents give 30 days / one month for grant of a new factory licence (BRAP-130, the Chief Inspectorate's process-flow sheet, and Order No. 1234/CIF &B/83/2019 as reproduced on the 'Time Bound Clearances' page), and BRAP-130 matches the ED's internal 20 + 5 + 5 split stage for stage. This directly answers the FGD complaint that 'there is no clear timeline for when the approval will be received' - the timeline is notified and published; the gap is dissemination, not policy.

Note on the gazette PDFs in the verified source list: the 2019 and 2020 gazette notifications (Part II No. 11 dated 26-2-2019 and Part II No. 53 dated 4-12-2020) are DRAFT rules published for objections under section 115(1) of the Factories Act, 1948. This session located and read the corresponding FINAL notifications on the Labour Department site and cited those instead where it mattered: G.O. Ms. No. 07/2019/Lab. dated 8 August 2019 (gazetted 9-8-2019) confirming the 2018 online-portal amendment, and G.O. Ms. No. 03/2020/Lab. dated 26 February 2021 (gazetted 2-3-2021) confirming the 2020 ten-year-validity and deemed-renewal amendment. The 2025 gazette (Part II No. 63 dated 7-8-2025) was fetched and read but concerns only Schedules II and III under rule 105 (prohibitions on employing pregnant women, lactating mothers and young persons in bath and lead processes) and bears on none of the five checked facts.

The file lrdeodbcifbfactories-act-amendment-2020.pdf linked from the B-Easy page as 'Draft Amendment to the Puducherry Factories Rules, 2020' returned HTTP 200 but is a structurally broken PDF reporting 0 pages, from which no text could be extracted; it yielded nothing and the same content was obtained from the gazette copy instead.

https://gras.py.gov.in/ (the fee-payment portal named in the rules and in BRAP-130) could NOT be fetched this session - curl returned 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' through the agent proxy - so it is not listed in sourcesRead even though it appears in the verified source list. The GRAS payment route is nevertheless confirmed by two documents that were read: BRAP-130 ('through online portal https://gras.py.gov.in') and the department's own 'Online Payment of Fees through GRAS ... for PLAN APPROVAL/LICENCE FEES/Medical Examination of workers under FACTORIES ACT, 1948' guideline (Version 2.0 dated 2 March 2018).

Nothing in any official source fetched this session addresses the FGD findings on informal payments, on preparing seven sets of documents, or on the absence of a single-window system for this licence; those remain uncorroborated and uncontradicted. (BRAP #112, the reform item behind the ServicePlus rollout, is itself headed 'Design and implement an online single window system ... without the requirement of physical visit to the department', which is the policy intent the FGD participants say they did not experience.)
